To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

• The HSP70 choperone machinery is the most versatile molecular machine in the cell • HSP70 chopeners are ubiquitous molecular chopenones that function in myriad biological processes, modulating polypeptide folding and translocation across membrances, protein–protein interactions and protein degradation.
• J proteins can bind directly to client proteins and deliver them to HSP70.

(a) the chaperone machinery is a complex, multicomponent system that is capable of binding a wide spectrum of client proteins; (b) the binding of client proteins by the chaperone system is not random, but is directed by the client proteins’ intrinsic properties; and (c) the client proteins’ properties are not the only determinant of their fate.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the molecular and cellular mechanisms that regulate the expression of the HSP genes in response to environmental stress, and the function of the HSPs in the maintenance of cellular protein quality.
the molecular mechanisms that control protein folding and aggregation.
the study of the molecular mechanisms of protein folding, misfolding and aggregation in vitro and in vivo.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the HSP70 system is a highly flexible and adaptable molecular machine that is capable of a broad range of activities, including folding, refolding, translocation and degradation, in the cell.
the J-protein family is the most diverse and complex group of HSP70 cofactors, and that they are essential for the regulation, targeting, and functional specificity of HSP70 activity in the cell.
J proteins determine the fate of clients by binding and delivering them to HSP70.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the HSP70 system is an extremely versatile chaperone system, which can be used for many different purposes, including protein folding, translocation, protein degradation, and even protein–protein interactions, depending on which cofactor is used.
the J proteins are the key players in the specificity of HSP70 function, and that the J proteins themselves are the key players for the specificity of the HSP90 function.
HSP70s are the central hub for protein folding, degradation and quality control.
The main takeaway from our work is that
J proteins can be viewed as drivers of specificity in the HSP70 chape- rone machinery, with each J protein having evolved to target specific clients to the chaperone.
HSP70s are not a homogeneous group of molecular chaperones but rather a diverse family of chaperones that perform a wide variety of cellular functions.
J protein cofactors are critical for HSP70 activity in vivo.
